specification.stock_exit: support minus 5% or 10%; 1.5R or 2R target; 40-session time exit; same-bar stop first
specification.market: SPY and QQQ point-in-time trend plus MACD
specification.heat: signal-day dollar-volume percentile and volume versus prior 20 sessions

specification.membership_policy: current ETF constituents were not backfilled historically

result: All four stock exit grids had positive profit factor and 1% trimmed expectancy overall and in each time split, but 2026 win rates and medians weakened. The 10%-buffer/2R grid returned PF 1.366/1.455/1.231 and trimmed expectancy 1.435%/2.085%/1.206% across development/2025/2026, while 2026 median was -0.707%. Risk-Off was near flat in development; Neutral outperformed the fixed Risk-On definition, so the market label is informative but not a validated hard gate. Relative volume >=2x improved development and 2025, but 2026 median was -2.339%, so it is a visibility candidate, not a score. Top-dollar-volume signal buckets underperformed the remaining signals and do not constitute alpha. Magnificent 7 was strong in development and 2025 but failed in 2026 with only 22 samples. Chip support stayed positive by trimmed expectancy in all three periods, though 2025 median was slightly negative. Theme ETF hotspots were positive in development and 2025 but failed in 2026: PF 0.630, trimmed expectancy -2.362%, median -2.214% on 70 events. Semiconductors and grid modernization were positive in all periods, but recent samples were too small to validate.
decision: Do not change production weights. Retain 5% and 10% support buffers plus 1.5R/2R as research grids; do not select a winner post hoc. Use Risk-Off as a caution flag rather than requiring Risk-On. Show high dollar volume for liquidity/attention only. Continue relative-volume >=2x, chip support, semiconductors and grid modernization as research candidates. Redesign industry heat to include constituent volume breadth and pullback/support position before retesting; begin forward stock-theme linkage from the dated 2026-08-26 membership snapshot.

change: Replace breakout-chasing market and industry contexts with predeclared pullback-at-support states; separately test MACD repair and volume recovery without changing the underlying stock signal or trade execution.
coverage: 52,327 fixed stock trades and 2,387 non-clustered industry ETF pullback scenarios; development through 2024, 2025 validation, 2026 forward observation

specification.stock_trade: strict rising long trend plus completed daily MACD cross; next Open; structural support minus 5%; 2R; 40 sessions; stop first
specification.market_pullback: SPY and QQQ long trends intact; either index 3%-12% below prior 60D high and within 3% of EMA20/50
specification.industry_pullback: ETF long trend intact; 5%-20% below prior 60D high and within 3% of an EMA below price
specification.macd_repair: histogram rises for two completed sessions
specification.volume_recovery: ETF volume at least 1.2 times prior 20-session average

result: Market pullback plus MACD repair was the strongest interpretable context overall: PF 1.753 and trimmed expectancy 2.491%; development/2025/2026 trimmed expectancy was 2.540%/3.435%/1.535%. The 2026 median remained -5.318%, so it is not a hard gate. Uptrend without pullback failed in 2026 with PF 0.920 and trimmed expectancy -0.656%. For industry ETFs, pullback at support produced PF 1.317 and trimmed expectancy 0.928% overall, remaining positive in development/2025/2026 at 0.944%/1.158%/0.460%. Adding MACD repair reduced overall results and failed in 2026; additionally requiring volume recovery was sample-thin and inconsistent. Compared with V1 trend-volume hotspots, whose 2026 trimmed expectancy was -2.362%, the pullback-at-support state was materially less fragile. Industry-level results remain mixed: semiconductor pullbacks with MACD and volume were positive overall, while digital assets and robotics pullbacks were weak.
decision: Promote pullback location to the primary research context for market and industry displays, but keep it outside official production score. Treat market pullback plus MACD repair as a candidate priority flag, not a buy gate. For industry, use long-trend pullback at support as the base state; show MACD and volume as descriptive evidence rather than mandatory additive factors. Continue dated forward stock-theme tracking before testing stock-level industry uplift.
